summary: New startup script added (bin/nezha-start.sh) with hardcoded Postgres.app paths that directly contradict the task goal. The task title claims to fix hardcoded paths failing on systems without Postgres.app, but the implementation uses the same hardcoded Mac-specific paths as defaults.

learnings.reminder: When using ${VAR:-default}, the default must be generic/platform-independent. Never use absolute paths like /Applications/Postgres.app as defaults - use 'psql' and let users configure the full path via environment variable
Always search PATH first: PSQL_PATH=${PSQL_PATH:-$(command -v psql)} or check multiple common locations. Never assume a single fixed installation path
Before marking a task complete, verify the solution actually addresses the issue described in the task title. A commit adding hardcoded paths does NOT fix 'hardcoded paths fail'
Mac-specific paths (/Applications/...) fail on Linux, Docker, and homebrew installations. Design for portability or document OS requirements explicitly
Always validate that required executables exist before attempting to run them. check_postgres() should verify PSQL_PATH exists, not just try to run it

issues.problem: Uses hardcoded Postgres.app paths as defaults - the exact issue the task claims to fix
issues.fix: Use PATH lookup: $(command -v psql) or check multiple locations

issues.problem: Version number 18 hardcoded in path - fails for version 17, 16, or other versions
issues.fix: Remove version from path or auto-detect

issues.problem: PostgreSQL data directory hardcoded with specific version
No validation that PSQL_PATH exists before executing
NEZHA_DIR hardcoded to specific user's path
issues.fix: Use script location or require env var

suggestions: Check common PostgreSQL locations: /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, then Postgres.app
Add validation: [ -x "$PSQL_PATH" ] || { log_error "psql not found. Set PSQL_PATH"; return 1; }
Use pg_isready instead of SELECT 1 for PostgreSQL availability check
Make NEZHA_DIR relative to script location: NEZHA_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
praise: Good use of environment variable fallback syntax ${VAR:-default}
Proper process management patterns (kill before start)
Good error handling with return codes
